url.description: The Alertmanager base URL, such as `http://alertmanager:9093`.

Assertion.description: One condition a probe result must meet, and the state a failure maps to.

banner.description: The text a TCP server sends after connecting (and after `send`).

certificate_days_remaining.description: Days until the server certificate expires.

chain_valid.description:
Whether the server certificate chains to a trusted root and is
within its validity period.

hostname_valid.description: Whether the server certificate is valid for the host name checked.

json.description: A value in the JSON response body.

on_fail.description: The state the check takes when this condition fails.

records.description: The records a DNS lookup returns.

status.description: The HTTP status is one of these.

Auth.description:
`[server.auth]`: how the admin page at `/admin/` learns who is asking.

tocsin never handles passwords. It sits behind an identity-aware proxy
and believes only what that proxy can prove: a signed Cloudflare Access
token, or a header from a peer address you trust. Without this table,
or with `mode = "none"`, the admin page does not exist.

allowed_domains.description:
Email domains allowed in, matched exactly (`example.com` does not
admit `team.example.com`).

allowed_emails.description:
Email addresses allowed in. With neither this nor
`allowed_domains`, everyone the proxy lets through is allowed.

audience.description:
`cloudflare_access` only: the Access application's audience (AUD)
tag.

header.description:
`trusted_header` only: the request header carrying the email
address. Defaults to `X-Forwarded-Email`.

mode.description: How identities are proven. `none` turns the admin page off.

team_domain.description:
`cloudflare_access` only: the Zero Trust team, as `name` or
`name.cloudflareaccess.com`.

oneOf.description:
Cloudflare Access: verify the signed `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion`
token against the team's published keys.
A proxy on a trusted network names the person in a header.

username.description: The user name. It may be a secret, `${ENV:NAME}`.

Check.description: A probe run on an interval, whose result sets a component's health.

assert.description:
Conditions a result must meet, each `[[check.assert]]` table holding
one. With none, a probe that completes counts as up, except that
`http` needs a 2xx or 3xx status, `dns` a `NOERROR` response and
`tls` a certificate that verifies for the host.

component.description: The `[[component]]` whose health this check sets.

confirm.description:
Consecutive results that disagree with the current state before the
state changes.

id.description:
Unique among checks and heartbeats in every file: they share one
history.

link.description:
Links shown with the check, such as its dashboard or runbook, each a
`[[check.link]]` table.

name.description: Display name; the id is shown when it is absent.

target.description:
What is probed. Its form depends on the type: a URL for `http`,
`host:port` for `tcp`, `host` or `host:port` for `tls`, a domain
name for `dns` and a host for `icmp`.

timeout.description:
How long one probe may take before it counts as failed. Must be
shorter than the interval.

oneOf.description: A TLS handshake, inspecting the certificate.

Cidr.description: An IP network such as "10.0.0.0/8" or "fd00::/8", or a single address such as "192.0.2.7".

Comparison.description: Numeric bounds; every bound given must hold.

Component.description: `[[component]]`: something the status page shows with a health state.

description.description: A line shown with the component.

group.description: The `[[group]]` the component is shown under.

id.description: Unique among components in every file.

rule.description: How the health of the component's checks combines into its own.

ComponentRule.description: How a component's health is derived from the health of its checks.

oneOf.description: The worst check decides: one check down makes the component down.

The worst state that more than half of the checks share or exceed:
one check down out of three leaves the component up.

resolver.description:
The resolver queried, as `ip` or `ip:port`; the system resolver when
absent.

FailureState.description: The state a failed assertion puts its check in.

oneOf.description: Working, but worse than it should be.

Group.description: `[[group]]`: a heading collecting components on the status page.

description.description: A line shown under the heading.

id.description: Unique among groups in every file.

HeaderAssertion.description: A condition on one response header.

contains.description: A value of the header contains this.

eq.description: A value of the header equals this.

name.description: The header name, matched without regard to case.

Heartbeat.description:
`[[heartbeat]]`: a ping tocsin expects to receive, such as a cron job
reporting in. Pings are sent to the write API with a token that has the
`heartbeat` scope. A heartbeat with no ping for `interval + grace` is
down; it is a member of its component exactly as a check is.

component.description: The `[[component]]` whose health this heartbeat sets.

grace.description:
How late a ping may be before the heartbeat is down: it is down once
`interval + grace` passes without one.

id.description:
Unique among checks and heartbeats in every file: they share one
history.

interval.description: How often a ping is expected.

link.description:
Links shown with the heartbeat, such as the job's logs or runbook,
each a `[[heartbeat.link]]` table.

name.description: Display name; the id is shown when it is absent.

body.description: Request body. It may be a secret, `${ENV:NAME}`.

follow_redirects.description: Whether redirects are followed; when not, a 3xx is the result.

headers.description: Request headers. A value may be a secret, `${ENV:NAME}`.

server_name.description:
The host name sent as TLS SNI and `Host`, and checked against the
certificate, when it differs from the target's host. The target's
host is still the address connected to.

verify_certificate.description:
Whether the server's certificate must verify. Defaults to true.
When false, the request proceeds and the certificate is still
reported, so `chain_valid` and `hostname_valid` can be asserted.

Id.description: A slug: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit.

JsonAssertion.description: A value selected from the JSON response body by an RFC 9535 JSON path.

contains.description: The value is a string containing this.

exists.description: Whether the path selects any value.

ne.description: The value does not equal this.

path.description:
An RFC 9535 JSON path, such as `$.checks[0].status` or
`$.components[?@.name=='API'].status`. When it selects several
values, the first in document order is compared.

Link.description:
A `[[check.link]]` or `[[heartbeat.link]]`: a named link to somewhere an
operator looks next, such as a dashboard, logs or a runbook. Also a
`[[page.link]]`, shown to everyone in the status page's header.

url.description: Where it goes: an absolute `http://` or `https://` URL.

Logo.description: `[page.logo]`: an image shown before the page title.

alt.description:
The image's text alternative. Leave it empty when the title beside
the logo already says what it shows.

url.description:
A path on this site, such as `"/brand/logo.svg"`, that the proxy in
front of tocsin serves. The page's content security policy loads
images from its own origin only, so a URL on another host would
not show.

Notifier.description:
A destination for operator alerts. Every alert it sends is followed by
a resolve with the same identity.

id.description: Unique among notifiers in every file.

max_in_flight.description:
The most deliveries this notifier sends at once. More wait for a
free slot, so a storm of alerts never floods the service.

name.description: Display name; the id is used when it is absent.

type.description:
Which service the notifier posts to; its settings go in the table of
the same name.

NotifierType.description: The service a notifier posts to.

token.description: An access token, for a protected topic. Secret.

endpoint.description:
The collector's base URL, such as `"http://otel-collector:4318"`.
Over `http/protobuf` the metrics go to its `/v1/metrics`. Without
it, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT` (used as is), then
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, then `http://localhost:4318`
(`http://localhost:4317` over `grpc`).

headers.description:
Headers sent with each export, such as an API key. A value may be
an `${ENV:NAME}` secret, which is never logged. They are added to
those in `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` and
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_HEADERS`; a header named in both is
sent with the value given here.

interval.description:
How often the metrics are sent. Without it,
`OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL` (milliseconds), then 60s.

resource.description:
Resource attributes added to those tocsin sets, such as
`{ "deployment.environment.name" = "production" }`. They win over
`OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, and `service.name` here wins over
`OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` and the default `"tocsin"`. `service.version` and
`service.instance.id` (the `node_id`) are tocsin's own and cannot be
set.

timeout.description:
How long one export may take before it is abandoned and counted as
failed. Without it, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TIMEOUT`, then
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT` (milliseconds), then 10s or `interval`,
whichever is shorter. It may not be longer than `interval`.

oneOf.description: Protobuf in an HTTP POST, to port 4318 by convention.

Page.description:
`[page]`: how the public status page looks, its title, logo, links,
the order of its groups and components, and the time zone it shows
times in.

accent.description:
The colour of links, buttons and the maintenance status, in hex
such as `"#0b5cad"`. It must reach WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) on the
light scheme's page background and surfaces. Unless `accent_dark`
is set, the dark scheme uses it mixed toward white until it reaches
4.5:1 on the dark backgrounds. Unset, the page uses its own blue.

accent_dark.description:
The accent in the dark colour scheme, in hex. It must reach 4.5:1
on the dark scheme's page background and surfaces. Unset, it is
derived from `accent`.

components.description:
The order components are shown in within their group, by id.
Components not listed follow in the order they are defined.

description.description: A line shown under the title.

groups.description:
The order groups are shown in, by id. Groups not listed follow in
the order they are defined.

homepage_url.description: Where the page's logo and title link to.

link.description:
Links in the page's header, such as the main site or a support
address, each a `[[page.link]]` table.

logo.description: The logo shown before the title, as `[page.logo]`.

timezone.description:
The time zone the page shows times in: an IANA name such as
`"Europe/Berlin"`. The uptime bars' days are UTC days regardless.

Project.description:
`[[project]]`: something whose releases and deploys the release log
records. CI pushes them; tocsin never polls.

components.description:
The `[[component]]`s this project's deploys belong to: a timeline
filtered to one of them shows them.

description.description: A line shown with the project.

id.description: Unique among projects in every file.

public.description:
Whether `/releases`, its feed and the unauthenticated API show the
project's releases. A non-public project's releases are seen only
with a `status:read` token or on the admin timeline.

degraded_priority.description: The priority of an alert that is degraded.

down_priority.description:
The Pushover priority, -2 to 2, of an alert that is down. 2 is an
emergency, repeated until acknowledged and cancelled by the resolve.

user_key.description: The user or group key alerts go to. Secret.

RecordsAssertion.description:
A condition on the records a DNS lookup returns. Records are compared
as text, ignoring a trailing `.` on names; CNAME, MX, NS and SRV
records, which hold names, also ignore case.

contains.description: One of the records equals this.

eq.description: The records are exactly these, in any order.

Route.description:
`[[route]]`: sends alerts matching its filters to its notifiers. Empty
filters match everything.

groups.description: Only alerts for components in these groups.

id.description: Unique among routes in every file.

notify_on.description:
The least severe state that alerts: `degraded` alerts on degraded and
down, `down` on down only.

repeat.description:
How often to send an alert again while it is still firing; `"0s"`
never repeats. Alertmanager notifiers re-post every minute whatever
this says, so Alertmanager never times the alert out.

Secret.description: A secret, read from an environment variable: "${ENV:NAME}".

auth.description: How the admin page authenticates people.

data_dir.description:
The folder holding the SQLite database. `tocsin serve --data`
overrides it.

email.description: Sender settings for every email tocsin sends.

listen.description:
The address the web server listens on, as `ip:port`: `127.0.0.1:8080`,
`0.0.0.0:8080` or `[::]:8080`. Hostnames are not accepted.

max_concurrent_checks.description:
The most checks that may run at once across the node. Checks due
while the limit is reached wait for a free slot.

node_id.description:
This node's name in every result it records. Defaults to the
hostname.

public_url.description: The URL people reach the status page at, used in links and emails.

ServerEmail.description:
`[server.email]`. Required, with `from`, `reply_to` and `smtp_url`,
whenever an email notifier exists.

Every email tocsin sends can be answered: neither address may be a
`noreply`, `no-reply` or `donotreply` address.

reply_to.description: The Reply-To address: a mailbox a person reads.

smtp_url.description:
The SMTP server, as `smtp://user:password@host:587` or
`smtps://...`. Secret.

Slack.description:
`[slack]`: your own Slack app, which people approve on Slack's consent
screen to connect a channel. Each connection is an incoming webhook,
kept in the database rather than in configuration.

With it, the admin page can connect channels for `[[notifier]]`s to
name with `connection`, and, with `[subscribers]`, visitors can add
status updates to their own Slack. `tocsin slack setup` prints the link
that creates the app. It needs an `https` `[server] public_url`, which
Slack sends people back to. Like `[server]`, it is read only at startup.

app_name.description:
The app's name, as Slack shows it on the consent screen and beside
each message, at most 35 characters. Used only by `tocsin slack
setup`; defaults to the page's title.

client_id.description: The app's Client ID, from its Basic Information page. Secret.

client_secret.description: The app's Client Secret, from the same page. Secret.

connection.description:
The name of a channel connected on the admin page's Slack tab,
with `[slack]`. A name not connected yet is a warning from `tocsin
config check`; an alert sent to it fails loudly.

webhook_url.description:
An incoming webhook URL you made yourself. Secret. Give this or
`connection`, not both.

Subscribers.description:
`[subscribers]`: lets people subscribe by email to incidents on the
components they choose and to the releases of public projects. Without
this table the page shows no form and the subscriber API answers 404.

It needs `[server] public_url`, for the links in each email, and a
complete `[server.email]` to send from. Like `[server]`, it is read only
at startup.

client_ip_header.description:
A header your proxy sets to the client's IP address, such as
`CF-Connecting-IP`. It is believed only when the TCP peer is inside
`trusted_proxies`; otherwise the peer's own address is the client's.

confirm_within.description:
How long a confirmation link works. An address not confirmed in
time is forgotten.

rate_window.description: The window both sign-up limits count over.

signups_per_email.description:
Sign-ups for one email address per `rate_window`, from anywhere.
Past it, a sign-up is refused with 429 and `Retry-After`.

signups_per_ip.description:
Sign-ups one client IP address may make per `rate_window`. Past
it, a sign-up is refused with 429 and `Retry-After`.

trusted_proxies.description:
The networks your proxy connects from. Required with
`client_ip_header`.

turnstile.description:
Cloudflare Turnstile on the sign-up form, as `[subscribers.turnstile]`.
With it, signing up needs JavaScript.

send.description:
Text written once connected, before the banner is read. Escapes such
as `\r\n` are written in TOML's own string syntax.

chat_id.description: The chat alerts are sent to.

Telemetry.description:
`[telemetry]`: where tocsin sends its own telemetry. Without it, it
sends none. Like `[server]`, it is read only at startup.

otlp.description:
`[telemetry.otlp]`: push the checks' metrics over OTLP. The table
turns the export on, even empty: each key it leaves out is taken
from the standard `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` environment variables, and
a key it sets wins over them.

Text.description: A string, or a secret read from an environment variable: "${ENV:NAME}".

not_contains.description: The text does not contain this.

regex.description:
The text matches this regular expression (Rust `regex` syntax),
anywhere in the text unless anchored with `^` or `$`.

server_name.description:
The server name sent in the handshake (SNI); the target's host when
absent.

Token.description: `[[token]]`: a bearer token for the write API.

description.description: Who or what uses the token.

id.description: Unique among tokens in every file; logged with each write.

oneOf.description:
Reading what is not public in the read API: checks and heartbeats
on no component, non-public projects' releases and deploys, check
targets, raw check results, and how the configuration last
reloaded. The internal board behind proxy auth reads the same.
Listing, counting and removing email subscribers.

Turnstile.description:
`[subscribers.turnstile]`: a Cloudflare Turnstile widget every sign-up
must pass.

secret_key.description:
The widget's secret key, which tocsin sends to Cloudflare to check
each answer. Secret.

site_key.description: The widget's site key, which the page shows.

signing_secret.description:
The key each body is signed with: HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp and
the body, sent in `X-Tocsin-Signature`. Secret.

url.description: The URL alerts are posted to as JSON.

description:
One configuration file. Every key is optional in a single file; rules
that span files (unique ids, references, required settings) are checked
after merging.

This is the type the JSON Schema describes.

component.description: What the status page shows, each with a health state.

group.description: Headings that collect components on the status page.

heartbeat.description: Pings tocsin expects to receive on an interval.

page.description: The public status page. At most one file may hold `[page]`.

project.description: Projects whose releases and deploys the release log records.

route.description: Which alerts go to which notifiers.

server.description: Server settings. At most one file may hold `[server]`.

slack.description:
Your Slack app, for connecting channels by signing in to Slack. At
most one file may hold `[slack]`; without it, channels cannot be
connected.

subscribers.description:
Email subscriptions on the public page. At most one file may hold
`[subscribers]`; without it, there are none.

telemetry.description:
Sending the checks' metrics to an OpenTelemetry collector. At most
one file may hold `[telemetry]`; without it, nothing is sent.

token.description: Bearer tokens for the write API.

title: tocsin configuration file
